techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities: Vulnerabilities
techniques.usage: Monitors the NIST National Vulnerability Database for vulnerability information to use in targeting. The joint advisory records more than forty CVEs researched this way - reading them, not necessarily exploiting them.

techniques.name: Develop Capabilities: Malware
techniques.usage: Builds and maintains its own RAT family rather than renting one: TigerRAT, SmallTiger, Dora RAT, ValidAlpha, LightHand, DurianBeacon, NukeSped, Atharvan and Goat RAT, written across C++ and Go and revised over years.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities: Tool
techniques.usage: Supplements the custom estate with off-the-shelf tooling: the Sliver C2 framework, Ngrok, masscan, 3Proxy, PuTTY and Mimikatz.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.usage: Exploits n-day vulnerabilities in internet-facing web servers, using public and custom exploits. Log4Shell is the example the advisory names; Confluence, PaperCut, TeamCity and Apache ActiveMQ are the other products recorded. This became the primary route in from around 2023.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.usage: The group's earlier lead technique, sending malicious attachments before the shift to exploitation. Retained rather than retired.

techniques.name: Drive-by Compromise
techniques.usage: Early operations used watering-hole attacks carrying zero-day exploits against South Korean visitors.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Client Execution
techniques.usage: Exploited ActiveX to run code on visitors to compromised sites - the execution half of the watering-hole operations.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.usage: Relies on the recipient opening the spear-phishing attachment to run the first stage.

techniques.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
techniques.usage: Plants web shells on the exploited web servers to hold the foothold and reach the applications and data behind it, independently of the exploit that got them there.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
techniques.usage: Packs the custom RAT family with the commercial protectors Themida and VMProtect before delivery.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Steganography
techniques.usage: Hid executable payload code inside PNG and BMP image files in early operations. ATT&CK cites this group by name as a procedure example for the technique.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.usage: Carries Mimikatz. Reporting names the tool without recording which credential store was read on any given intrusion, so this stays at the parent technique rather than asserting LSASS.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.usage: Took 1.2 TB from South Korean defence contractors in December 2023. Reporting records the volume rather than the stores it came from, so this is the outcome-level claim that data was taken off compromised systems.

techniques.name: Input Capture: Keylogging
techniques.usage: TigerRAT logs keystrokes. Placed under Collection rather than Credential Access because the reporting frames the capability as watching an operator work rather than as harvesting logons.

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.usage: TigerRAT records the screen, which for a collection mandate built around drawings and design documents returns material a file grab would miss.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.usage: Runs Sliver implants against defence and aerospace targets. Reporting names the framework without specifying the protocol chosen, so this stays at the parent technique.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.usage: Uses 3Proxy and other SOCKS proxies to relay operator traffic.

techniques.name: Remote Access Tools
techniques.usage: Abuses legitimate remote monitoring and management software already trusted in the estate, so the operator channel is signed administrative tooling rather than a custom implant.

techniques.name: Protocol Tunneling
techniques.usage: Uses Ngrok to tunnel out of networks that would otherwise not permit an inbound connection.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.usage: Deploys Maui ransomware against US healthcare, encrypting servers running diagnostics, electronic health records and imaging. This is the funding arm rather than the objective - the proceeds pay for the collection operations against everyone else.
